subject: Inference pathway qualification & proposed cutover plan
messages:
From: alex_martinez@redwood.ai
To: Priya Shah <priya@acme.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 03 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up: inference pathway & next steps after today's discovery

Hi Priya / Michael —

Thanks for taking the time today. Quick recap from our discovery so everyone has the same view and we can align next steps: 

- Primary objective: replace ACME's legacy GPU cluster for customer-facing NLU models (low latency, SLAs, multi-tenant usage) and consolidate a second batch job workload used for nightly batch embeddings.
- Throughput target: ~200 concurrent low-latency streams (95th p95 < 300ms), and 4M tokens/day across product calls.
- Data requirements: customer PII is logged in requests; need encryption-at-rest + ability to isolate request data (audit logs).
- Migration constraints: current stack uses an older self-hosted LLM serving layer (custom cluster) + occasional calls to a third-party API for burst traffic. Want minimal user-facing downtime and a pilot inside their VPC if possible.

Initial hosting fit thoughts (for internal reference):
- Hosted API: fastest path, simple auth + streaming; concerns around data residency and audit evidence unless we use Private routing + export controls.
- Dedicated capacity: good middle ground — predictable throughput and ability to pin model variants; possible for pilot if we can provide a private peering option.
- Private (VPC/on-prem): best for strict compliance (audit logs + KMS/HSM) but longer timeline (network setup, compliance sign-off).

Next steps I propose:
1) ACME to confirm which environment they prefer for the pilot (Hosted w/controls | Dedicated w/peering | Private VPC).
2) ACME to share a short ACL + example request payloads (anonymized) so we can estimate cost and sizing.
3) Redwood to produce a migration cutover options memo and a Pilot SOW draft (we'll include a fall-back plan to keep legacy cluster during cutover).

I've attached an initial migration matrix template and a SOW skeleton to accelerate the pilot discussion. Happy to jump on another call this week to go over the tradeoffs if helpful.

Cheers,
Alex Martinez
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Thanks Alex — this looks right based on our call. A few clarifications from our side: 

1) For the pilot we'd prefer Dedicated with private peering if the timeline can be under 4 weeks. We want to keep traffic inside our cloud account for initial customer-facing tests.
2) We need contract language covering: SOC2 evidence, data deletion guarantees, KMS integration (customer-managed keys).
3) Migration constraints: we can't change the model architecture for the first release; we need a functionally equivalent model served with identical tokenization and prompt interfaces.

Hi Priya —

Appreciate the preference for Dedicated + peering. A couple of technical notes to set expectations for a 4-week pilot timeline: 

- Network onboarding: Private peering requires an account IP exchange and 2–3 business days to provision once Paperwork is signed. If ACME uses a cloud provider's VPC peering + Shared VPC setup we can compress setup time.
- Model parity: we can support runtime-compatible endpoints if you can share model artifacts or the tokenizer + sample sequences. If we need to convert weights (quantize/optimize), that usually adds 1–2 weeks depending on model size.
- Data controls: we support customer-managed KMS and per-tenant audit logs. SOC2 artifacts can be shared under NDA; we have a packaged SOC2 plus supplementary audit evidence for Dedicated customers.

If ACME confirms Dedicated for pilot, we (Redwood) will: provide a dedicated capacity estimate, outline required network configuration, and deliver a Pilot SOW draft that includes a rollback plan to the legacy cluster.

Would you and Michael be available for a 30-minute technical sync Wed or Thu?

Best,
Marissa Cole
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai

From: alex_martinez@redwood.ai

Date: Tue, 06 Apr 2027 15:44:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: inference pathway & next steps after today's discovery

Priya / Michael —

Thanks for confirming the preference. Proposed immediate plan: 

1) Pilot on Dedicated with private peering (target kickoff: Apr 26). Deliverables before kickoff: signed Pilot SOW, short network worksheet, and anonymized payloads + model spec from ACME.
2) Redwood will scope a migration cutover with two tracks: (A) parallel run behind a feature flag (traffic mirrored for validation), and (B) canary routing (5% traffic -> 25% -> 100%) with automatic fallback to legacy cluster for first 72 hours.
3) Timeline assumptions are: network peering docs signed in week 1; infra provisioning and capacity tuning in week 2; integration + test window week 3; canary cutover week 4.

I attached the migration matrix again with a column called "cutover risk" filled based on our discussion — this should help ACME pick the pilot boundaries. Please review and let me know if Apr 26 kickoff is feasible from your side. If you prefer, we can move to a Hosted pilot while peering is provisioned but keep data isolation controls enabled.
